## Data Model
No data model changes required. Settings JSON keys are unchanged; only the rule strings differ.

## API Contracts
`hefesto-setup.sh --check` gains one entry in its `missing` list, in the style of `:272`'s "no sandbox write grant
that reaches …": `no ask rule outside the signature set (<rule> in <file> — every lane pass would stop on it)`, so the
printed line reads `setup: missing no ask rule outside the signature set (…) for <root> — run: …`. The test greps
`no ask rule outside the signature set (` plus the rule. Options and exit codes are unchanged.
The defect pass classifies a rule by its subcommand and flag (the tail's first word after `ledger.sh`, plus a
signature flag when present), not by the exact string: a mechanics subcommand gets the message above; a
signature written in a non-canonical form (`Bash(<h>/ledger.sh approve)`, no `:*`) is not reported as a mechanic —
it is reported, if at all, only by the existing missing-signature check under this root's spelling. So the message
is never false for a signature (round 4, item 6).

## Implementation Approach
1. **One classification, in setup.** Four bash arrays near the top of the rule section: `LEDGER_SIGN_WHOLE`
   (approve answer revise drop fold supersede reopen "op close" "op drop"), `LEDGER_SIGN_FLAG`
   ("unblock --reviewed-by-human" "unblock --merge-sha" "record --body-file" "record --body-from-board"
   "record --rfc" "release --reviewed-by-human"), `LEDGER_LAUNCHER` (claim run — no rule written), `LEDGER_ALLOW`
   (every other dispatch arm, with today's narrower forms kept: `park --all`, `op new`, `dir`). `pr-watch.sh reply|comment` stay as they are. These lists are the single source the writer,
   `--check` and the test read.
2. **One spelling per root.** `roots` gains a parallel `kinds` array (clone | installed). Installed roots are
   added first and the clone last, so a root that is both (setup run from the installed copy) keeps `installed`.
   The reorder changes `${roots[0]}`, which setup reads outside the loop for the context-gauge `statusLine`
   command (`:232`) and its hint (`:385`): those use `gauge_root` — `$CLONE` when it is in `roots`, else
   `${roots[0]}` — so the status line keeps a release-stable path (today's behaviour) rather than a
   version-pinned cache folder that the next `plugin update` deletes. `hooks_of <root> <kind>`
   prints `<root>/hooks` for the clone and `<root>//hooks` for an installed copy (D4). The rule loop runs once
   per root with that `h`; the `bash $h` ask spelling is dropped. Exclusions use the same `h`.
3. **Writing.** ask = `Bash($h/ledger.sh <s>:*)` for each WHOLE entry, `Bash($h/ledger.sh <sub> * <flag>*)` for each
   FLAG entry; allow = `Bash($h/ledger.sh <s>:*)` for each ALLOW entry (exact forms where today's are exact).
   Strip-then-add is unchanged, so old spellings, stale versions and mechanics asks leave on the first run.
4. **`--check`.** (a) the kind of `me` (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$CLONE}` with its trailing `/` removed, `:239`) is
   looked up in the `roots`/`kinds` arrays setup itself built (installed wins, step 2): `me` equal to an installed
   root → installed, else equal to `$CLONE` → clone. **`me` in neither** (an untrusted or skipped root — inside the project or a temp folder, or a
   profile setup never saw) → `--check` reports `the hefesto folder this session runs from (<me>) is not one setup
   trusts` and exits 1; it never guesses a spelling. The signature asks must then exist under `hooks_of "$me" <kind>`,
   one rule each (replacing `:241-243`); the allow check (`:241`) and both exclusion checks (`:244-245`) read the
   same `hooks_of "$me" <kind>` instead of `--arg h "$me/hooks"` (`:240`). (b) the defect pass is folded into the existing three-file loop
   (`:275-284`, `$F`, `$TOP/.claude/settings.json`, the profile's `settings.json`) — one more `jq` per file: each
   `permissions.ask` rule that names a hefesto helper is normalised to its tail (`ledger.sh approve:*`,
   `ledger.sh unblock * --merge-sha*`) and any tail not among the signature tails is added to `miss` with its file
   (message: API Contracts). Exit 1, as every other `--check` miss. A leftover `claim`/`run` ask is a defect like
   any other mechanics ask.
   (c) **Launcher-only `claim`/`run` (FR-010).** `session-launch.sh` already unsets `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` before
   its ledger calls (`hooks/session-launch.sh:56`); it now also passes `HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1` on each of its six
   `$LEDGER claim|run` calls. One more production caller exists: `handoff` re-enters the ledger with
   `bash "$0" run "$ID" --role implement …` (`hooks/ledger.sh:787`) — the ledger's own record of a hand-run, not a
   session's `run`; it becomes `env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1 bash "$0" run …` with a comment.
   `handoff` already refuses an owned entry (`:767`), so this frees no lane's claim; FR-010 reads "unless
   `session-launch.sh` — or `handoff`'s own re-entry — calls them". Regression: `tests/smoke.sh:3242-3244` (the
   handoff happy path); mutant: marker dropped from `:787` → that test red. **The marked re-entry is safe only
   because the arm first refuses a lanes session** (round 5): today a lane's `handoff` dies at `caller_gate:262` on
   the inner `run` (the session id is inherited); with the marker it would pass, letting any interactive lane take an
   unowned item to `pr` with no dialog. So the `handoff` arm, before its owner write (`:784`), calls a small
   `in_lanes_session` helper — `caller_gate`'s own preamble (`valid_sid` → `session_file` exists → `.lanes == true`,
   `:259-261`) lifted into a function that `caller_gate` keeps its exact behaviour around — and dies
   `ledger handoff <id>: a hand command — a lane finishes with session-launch.sh --finish`, nothing written.
   The `:787` comment says the session id is dropped *because* the arm already refused lane sessions. (The re-entries at `:788-790,822` and
   `hooks/ledger-recipes.sh:258` are `record|advance|block`, not launcher-only — untouched.) A new `launcher_gate`, called right after `caller_gate` at `hooks/ledger.sh:390` (so a lane session still gets
   `caller_gate`'s lane message, `:262`, and every other caller reaches this check), dies when:
   `is_launcher_sub "$SUB"` and not (`HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1` with `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` empty) → die naming
   `session-launch.sh` (and `ledger.sh release` for a person freeing a claim), nothing written. A Claude session
   cannot forge it: its Bash commands carry `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and in a set-up project `lane-guard.sh:104-109`
   denies a leading assignment, `env` wrapper or chain on an excluded helper; outside setup `ledger.sh` is not
   sandbox-excluded and its write fails (`hooks/ledger.sh:237`). A person in a terminal is refused too (the answer
   says launcher-only); `release` stays their tool. The marker is a brake against sessions, not a secret: a person
   in a terminal can type it, and the docs/CHANGELOG claim no more. Each of the six call sites carries a comment:
   the marker is per call, never `export`ed beside `:56`, because the `claude` worker the launcher spawns
   (`:625`) would inherit an exported one.
5. **Tests** (part 11 — `tests/smoke.sh:6711` already sources part 10 — `tests/smoke-signatures.sh`):
   - **SC-001** fixture reduction (Sketch 5), exact `permissions.ask` result; mutants: re-add the `//` spelling for
     the clone / the `bash ` spelling → red.
   - **SC-002** `--check` defect: inject `Bash(<h>/ledger.sh claim:*)` in `$F`, and separately in the profile's

   - **FR-005 kind lookup**: a fake profile whose `installed_plugins.json` lists `$REPO` itself as the user-scope
     `installPath` (trusted — not under `mktemp -d`, so `unsafe_root` keeps it, `tests/smoke.sh:5447,5489`); this is
     the production case of `--check` running from the installed copy (`CLONE` = that path). Setup writes; then
     `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=$REPO/ --check` passes and the written asks are under `$REPO//hooks`. Mutants: `hooks_of`
     always single-slash → red; the clone added before the installed roots (clone kind wins) → red. And
     `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=/elsewhere --check` exits 1 naming the untrusted folder. The same run asserts
     `.statusLine.command` starts with `$REPO/hooks/` (`gauge_root`); mutant: `gauge_root` = `${roots[0]}` with a
     second installed root listed first → red.
   - **FR-010 / SC-007 launcher-only**: in a project set up without `--lanes`, `ledger.sh claim <id>` with a fake
     `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` → non-zero, message names `session-launch.sh`, entry unchanged; `HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1`
     with the session id still set → refused; `run` likewise; the **terminal case** the person decided — no
     `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, no marker (`env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID bash …/ledger.sh claim …`) → non-zero,
     output names `session-launch.sh` and `release`, entry byte-identical (the rewritten
     `smoke-lifecycle-ops.sh:295`); the hook half of the forgery defence — through `gd`,
     `env -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1 $LGL claim …` → `deny`, beside the existing
     `tests/smoke.sh:5624` pattern; `--prepare` (the existing `tests/smoke.sh:6222-6225` case) still claims. **Lane `handoff`** (round 5): `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=<a sid with a lanes session record>` +
     `ledger.sh handoff <id> --pr <url>` on an unowned, unblocked item at `implement` → non-zero, output names
     `--finish`, entry byte-identical (no `owner: hand` left); mutant: the arm's lanes refusal removed → red. The
     `lsl handoff` calls at `tests/smoke.sh:3236,3238,3240,3242` run with the sid unset (terminal shape), per the
     P3 rule. Mutants: the `launcher_gate` call removed → red; the marker dropped from
     `session-launch.sh:580` → the `--prepare` case red.
     **P3 rule for the existing refusal assertions:** every existing "must be refused" `claim`/`run` call
     (`tests/smoke.sh:1939,2567,5853,5897,5899,5904`; `tests/smoke-lifecycle-ops.sh:309`) runs **marked** with the
     session id unset, so only the guard under test (stall count, per-repo lock, worker guard, stage limits, op
     rule, `--pid`+`--mode`) can refuse it — never FR-010; `:5853` (`HEFESTO_WORKER=1 bash "$LG" run …`) stays refused
     for the worker reason with the marker added. `:6140` and `:6232` set a lane session id and stay refused by the
     lane rules (`hooks/ledger.sh:262`, `lane-guard.sh`), and keep the lane message: the FR-010 check is a separate
     `launcher_gate`, called right after `caller_gate` at `:390` — `caller_gate` (unchanged) dies first for a lane
     session with its lane message; every other caller falls through its early returns to `launcher_gate`. Both

   - **SC-004** classification completeness. The subcommand source is the union of (i) the `usage` text
     (`hooks/ledger.sh:27-65`, first word of each listed form, `|`-separated alternatives split), (ii) the pre-case

   - **FR-007 ↔ FR-001**: source `hooks/lane-lib.sh`, loop over every `LEDGER_SIGN_WHOLE`/`LEDGER_SIGN_FLAG` form and

   - **SC-003** grammar table: a small matcher implementing the documented grammar (deny→ask→allow, `*` = any text,

     `record|unblock|release`, `advance`, `handoff`, `block`, `verdict` allow; `claim`/`run` match no rule. Mutant: drop the `record * --body-file*`

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: the classification lists
**File:** `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (modify at `:120`)
**Intent:** one source for writer, `--check` and tests.

```bash
# HEF-27: a dialog only where a person signs. Everything else in ledger.sh's dispatch is allowed, one by one —
# never ledger.sh as a whole, so a new subcommand is classified before it runs without asking (FR-006).
LEDGER_SIGN_WHOLE=(approve answer revise drop fold supersede reopen "op close" "op drop")
LEDGER_SIGN_FLAG=("unblock --reviewed-by-human" "unblock --merge-sha" "record --body-file" "record --body-from-board" "record --rfc"
  "release --reviewed-by-human")   # it records a person's name → a signature (spec Clarifications 2026-11-09)
LEDGER_LAUNCHER=(claim run)        # no rule at all: ledger.sh refuses them unless session-launch.sh calls (FR-010)
LEDGER_ALLOW=(board list next show metrics register publish escalate questions request actions action "op new" direct
  directives directive note lanes deployed record advance handoff block release unblock verdict init where branches spec-roots)
LEDGER_ALLOW_EXACT=("park --all" dir)
```

**Why this shape:** D1/D3; the test diffs these against the subcommand source of step 5 (SC-004).

### Sketch 2: one spelling per root
**File:** `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (modify `:105-121`)
**Intent:** the spelling `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks` produces for each root kind (D4).

```bash
roots=(); kinds=()
add_root() { local p="${1%/}" k="$2"; [ -n "$p" ] || return 0
  if unsafe_root "$p"; then skipped+=("$p"); return 0; fi
  case " ${roots[*]-} " in *" $p "*) ;; *) roots+=("$p"); kinds+=("$k") ;; esac; }
# … add_root "$p" installed for each installPath FIRST, then:
add_root "$CLONE" clone   # deduped: run from the installed copy, CLONE is that path and stays `installed`
hooks_of() { [ "$2" = installed ] && printf '%s//hooks' "$1" || printf '%s/hooks' "$1"; }  # tests/smoke.sh:860-862
for i in "${!roots[@]}"; do h="$(hooks_of "${roots[$i]}" "${kinds[$i]}")"
```

**Why this shape:** keeps `$h` (the github-board mutant seds it) and the rest of the loop body intact.

### Sketch 3: the rules written
**File:** `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (replace `:133-135`)

```bash
  for s in "${LEDGER_SIGN_WHOLE[@]}"; do ask+=("Bash($h/ledger.sh $s:*)"); done
  # the flag anywhere after the id (D7); `record * --rfc*` also matches the launcher-only --rfc-snapshot: an over-ask
  for s in "${LEDGER_SIGN_FLAG[@]}"; do ask+=("Bash($h/ledger.sh ${s% *} * ${s#* }*)"); done
  for s in "${LEDGER_ALLOW[@]}"; do allow+=("Bash($h/ledger.sh $s:*)"); done
  for s in "${LEDGER_ALLOW_EXACT[@]}"; do allow+=("Bash($h/ledger.sh $s)"); done
```

**Why this shape:** ask outranks allow, so `record:*` in allow and `record * --body-file*` in ask coexist (D7).

### Sketch 4: `--check`'s defect pass
**File:** `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (inside the existing three-file loop at `:275-284`)

```bash
sign_tails="$(sign_tails_json)"   # before the loop: ["ledger.sh approve:*", "ledger.sh unblock * --merge-sha*", "pr-watch.sh reply:*", …]
  # … inside `for sf in "$F" "$TOP/.claude/settings.json" "<cfg>/settings.json"`, beside the sandbox.enabled check:
  while IFS= read -r r; do miss="${miss:+$miss, }no ask rule outside the signature set ($r in $sf — every lane pass would stop on it)"
  done < <(jq -r --argjson t "$sign_tails" '(.permissions.ask // [])[] | strings
      | select(test("^Bash\\((bash )?/.*/hooks/(ledger|pr-watch|session-launch|status-board|speckit-helper|run-follow|hefesto-setup)\\.sh"))
      | select((sub("^Bash\\((bash )?.*/hooks/"; "") | rtrimstr(")")) as $x | $t | index([$x]) | not)' "$sf")
  # (the loop's own `done` follows the existing checks)
```

**Precision (round 5):** the exact-tail `index([$x])` above is illustrative; the implementation classifies by
subcommand + signature flag as API Contracts states, so a non-canonical signature ask is never called a mechanic.

**Why this shape:** reports by helper basename, any prefix, so a rule under a moved clone or a removed profile is
still found (D6: reported, never edited outside `$F`).

### Sketch 5: the 408-rule fixture, generated
**File:** `tests/smoke-signatures.sh` (new)

```bash
sg_old() { # $1 hooks dir → the 9.3 rule set for it: 17 asks × 2 spellings + pr-watch, and the old allows
  for c in unblock record claim advance handoff block revise answer approve release drop fold supersede reopen "op close" "op drop"; do
    printf 'Bash(%s/ledger.sh %s:*)\nBash(bash %s/ledger.sh %s:*)\n' "$1" "$c" "$1" "$c"; done; }
for h in "$REPO/hooks" "$REPO//hooks" "$sg_home/.claude/plugins/cache/hefesto/hefesto/9.3.0/hooks" "…//hooks" "…/9.2.0/hooks"; do sg_old "$h"; done \
  | jq -R . | jq -s '{permissions: {ask: (. + ["Bash(rm -rf:*)"]), allow: ["Bash(ls)"]}}' > "$sg_p/.claude/settings.local.json"
```

**Placement (round 5):** `$sg_home` and every fake installed root sit where `unsafe_root` accepts them (beside the
repo, the `l3_su_mut` pattern, `tests/smoke.sh:5425-5429`), never under `$TMPDIR` — otherwise setup skips them and
the "two live roots" expectation is red for the wrong reason.

**Why this shape:** the shape is the 9.3 writer's, so the fixture is generated (same spellings, same counts: 17 × 2
× 5 hooks dirs = 170 ledger asks, plus the allows) rather than a 900-line file kept in sync by hand. The test
asserts the result exactly: `permissions.ask` = the signature set under the two live roots' canonical spellings
plus the person's `Bash(rm -rf:*)`, nothing else.

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **Principle 1** (payload not under `.claude/`): no new payload directory; tests and hooks at the root.
- [x] **Principle 2** (namespaced commands): no command added.
- [x] **Principle 3** (mutation-tested, tool-call level): every new assertion has a mutant (re-add `bash`/`//`
  spelling; drop the defect pass; drop a FLAG entry; add an unclassified arm); the grammar is also checked against
  the live matcher, and the `--prepare` test asserts on the launcher's own `$LEDGER` calls.
- [x] **Principle 4** (zero-install): bash + jq only.
- [x] **Principle 5** (fail loudly): `--check` exits 1 naming rule and file; a call in an unwritten spelling is not
  sandbox-excluded and its ledger write fails loudly (`hooks/ledger.sh:237`) instead of running unasked.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| The real matcher does not honour a mid-pattern `*` as documented | a flagged signature is allowed by `unblock:*`/`record:*` with no dialog | the live-tier grammar check (SC-003) runs before release; fallback is one line each: put `unblock` and `record` back in `LEDGER_SIGN_WHOLE` |
| The installed copy's spelling is single-slash on some Claude Code version | its helper calls are not sandbox-excluded → ledger writes fail loudly | `--check` at session start reports the missing set for this root; the live tier asserts the spelling; fallback: `hooks_of` prints both for installed roots |
| A person relied on a mechanics ask as a brake | they lose that dialog | the CHANGELOG names it; `ledger.sh` still refuses person decisions from lanes |
| `hefesto-setup.sh` grows past 500 code lines | commit blocked | today 388 non-blank lines; the change is about +35 net |
| A person who ran `ledger.sh claim` by hand loses it | refused with a message | the message names `session-launch.sh` and `release`; the CHANGELOG names it (the person's decision) |
| A session forges the launcher marker | `claim`/`run` outside the launcher | set-up project: `lane-guard.sh:64,104-109` denies the assignment/wrapper; no setup but sandbox on: the write fails (`hooks/ledger.sh:237`); no setup and no sandbox: no brake — the same as today (no rule exists there either); the CHANGELOG says exactly this |
| A test calls `claim`/`run` without the marker | red suite after FR-010 | the `tests/smoke.sh` sites set it; the full suite runs in the task that adds the check |
| `--check` now reads user settings with someone's own hefesto-looking ask rules | session start shows a miss | the message names the file; it is the defect the item asks to surface |

## Quick Start
1. Add the classification lists and `hooks_of` (Sketches 1–3); run `tests/smoke.sh` and update the two
   assertions that pin the old spellings.
2. Write `tests/smoke-signatures.sh` with the fixture reduction and its mutant (red first).
3. Add the `--check` defect pass (Sketch 4) with its test and mutant.
4. Completeness, grammar table, `--prepare` regression; live tier; docs.
